ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=6$, and $AB=10$. Point D moves from point B in the direction of ray BC at a speed of $5$ units per second, and point F moves from point A towards point B along edge AB at the same speed. When F reaches point B, point D stops moving. Let the movement time of point D be $t$ seconds. A square $DEFG$ is constructed with $DF$ as its diagonal. During the movement, if one side of square $DEFG$ happens to coincide with one side of the right-angled triangle $ABC$, then what is the value of $t$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given that in the right triangle $ABC$, $AC=6$ and $AB=10$, \\
$\therefore BC=\sqrt{AB^2-AC^2}=8$, \\
because point $D$ moves from point $B$ in the direction of ray $BC$ at a speed of 5 units per second, and point $F$ moves from point $A$ towards point $B$ along edge $AB$ at the same speed, \\
$\therefore AF=DB=5t$, \\
As shown in the figure, taking $B$ as the origin and the line along $BC$ as the x-axis, a Cartesian coordinate system is established, \\
$\therefore A(8,6)$ \\
Let the equation of line $BA$ be $y=kx$, then $6=8k$ \\
Solving gives $k=\frac{3}{4}$, \\
$\therefore$ the equation of line $BA$ is $y=\frac{3}{4}x$, \\
Let $F(m,\frac{3}{4}m)$, $0\le m\le 8$, \\
(1) As shown in the figure, when $DE$ is on side $BC$, draw $FM\perp AC$ at $M$. \\
$\therefore FM=8-m$, $AM=6-\frac{3}{4}m$, \\
$\therefore AF^2=AM^2+FM^2=\left(8-m\right)^2+\left(6-\frac{3}{4}m\right)^2=\left(\frac{5m-40}{4}\right)^2$, \\
because $AF=5t$, \\
$\therefore 5t=\left|\frac{5m-40}{4}\right|$, \\
Solving gives $t=\left|\frac{m-8}{4}\right|$, \\
because $0\le m\le 8$, \\
$\therefore t=\frac{8-m}{4}$ \\
$\therefore$ $FM=EC=4t$, $AM=3t$, $CM=EF=DE=6-3t$, \\
because $BD+DE+EC=8$, \\
$\therefore$ $5t+6-3t+4t=8$, \\
Solving gives $t=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$, \\
(2) As shown in the figure, when $FG$ is on side $AB$, \\
In right triangle $\triangle BGD$, with $DB=5t$, similar to (1) we can conclude $DG=FG=3t$, then $BG=4t$, \\
because $BG+FG+AF=10$, \\
$\therefore$ $4t+3t+5t=10$, \\
Solving gives $t=\frac{5}{6}$, \\
(3) When $DG$ is on side $BC$, \\
then $FG=DG=6-3t$, $BG=8-4t$, \\
because $BD=BG+DG=5t$, \\
$\therefore$ $8-4t+6-3t=5t$, \\
Solving gives $t=\frac{7}{6}$; \\
(4) When $EF$ is on side $AB$, \\
Similar to (1) we can conclude $BE=4t$, $DE=EF=3t$, \\
because $BE-EF=BF$, \\
$\therefore$ $4t-3t=10-5t$, \\
Solving gives $t=\frac{5}{3}$; \\
In summary, $t=\frac{1}{3}$ or $\frac{5}{6}$ or $\frac{7}{6}$ or $\frac{5}{3}$.

During the movement, if one side of square $DEFG$ happens to coincide with one side of the right-angled triangle $ABC$, then what is the value of $t$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given that in the right triangle $ABC$, $AC=6$ and $AB=10$, \\ $\therefore BC=\sqrt{AB^2-AC^2}=8$, \\ because point $D$ moves from point $B$ in the direction of ray $BC$ at a speed of 5 units per second, and point $F$ moves from point $A$ towards point $B$ along edge $AB$ at the same speed, \\ $\therefore AF=DB=5t$, \\ As shown in the figure, taking $B$ as the origin and the line along $BC$ as the x-axis, a Cartesian coordinate system is established, \\ $\therefore A(8,6)$ \\ Let the equation of line $BA$ be $y=kx$, then $6=8k$ \\ Solving gives $k=\frac{3}{4}$, \\ $\therefore$ the equation of line $BA$ is $y=\frac{3}{4}x$, \\ Let $F(m,\frac{3}{4}m)$, $0\le m\le 8$, \\ (1) As shown in the figure, when $DE$ is on side $BC$, draw $FM\perp AC$ at $M$. \\ $\therefore FM=8-m$, $AM=6-\frac{3}{4}m$, \\ $\therefore AF^2=AM^2+FM^2=\left(8-m\right)^2+\left(6-\frac{3}{4}m\right)^2=\left(\frac{5m-40}{4}\right)^2$, \\ because $AF=5t$, \\ $\therefore 5t=\left|\frac{5m-40}{4}\right|$, \\ Solving gives $t=\left|\frac{m-8}{4}\right|$, \\ because $0\le m\le 8$, \\ $\therefore t=\frac{8-m}{4}$ \\ $\therefore$ $FM=EC=4t$, $AM=3t$, $CM=EF=DE=6-3t$, \\ because $BD+DE+EC=8$, \\ $\therefore$ $5t+6-3t+4t=8$, \\ Solving gives $t=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$, \\ (2) As shown in the figure, when $FG$ is on side $AB$, \\ In right triangle $\triangle BGD$, with $DB=5t$, similar to (1) we can conclude $DG=FG=3t$, then $BG=4t$, \\ because $BG+FG+AF=10$, \\ $\therefore$ $4t+3t+5t=10$, \\ Solving gives $t=\frac{5}{6}$, \\ (3) When $DG$ is on side $BC$, \\ then $FG=DG=6-3t$, $BG=8-4t$, \\ because $BD=BG+DG=5t$, \\ $\therefore$ $8-4t+6-3t=5t$, \\ Solving gives $t=\frac{7}{6}$; \\ (4) When $EF$ is on side $AB$, \\ Similar to (1) we can conclude $BE=4t$, $DE=EF=3t$, \\ because $BE-EF=BF$, \\ $\therefore$ $4t-3t=10-5t$, \\ Solving gives $t=\frac{5}{3}$; \\ In summary, $t=\frac{1}{3}$ or $\frac{5}{6}$ or $\frac{7}{6}$ or $\frac{5}{3}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, the base BC of right triangle ABC is a horizontal line, AC is a vertical side, and the right angle is at C; the hypotenuse AB connects from B at the lower left to A at the upper right. Point D is located on the horizontal ray from B along the direction of BC, point F is located on the hypotenuse AB, and square DEFG is constructed with DF as the diagonal; one schematic position of the square in the figure shows D and E near the lower side, F on AB, and G on the upper left side.

Then reason: From AC=6, AB=10, obtain BC=sqrt(10^2-6^2)=8. Establish a coordinate system according to the method: B=(0,0), C=(8,0), A=(8,6), so the equation of AB is y=3x/4. Point D moves from B along the ray BC, with speed 5, so D=(5t,0). Point F moves from A along AB toward B, AF=5t, and the unit direction vector of AB from A to B is (-4/5,-3/5), so F=(8-4t,6-3t), and 0<=t<=2.

Let v=F-D=(8-9t,6-3t). According to the square direction shown in the figure, take the side vector from D to E as DE=(v+R_clockwise(v))/2=(7-6t,3t-1). Therefore E=D+DE=(7-t,3t-1). The other side vector from D to G is R_90(DE)=(1-3t,7-6t), so G=(1+2t,7-6t).

Check one by one the cases where a side of the square coincides with a side of the triangle:
1. DE is on BC: because D is already on y=0, only need E_y=0, namely 3t-1=0, obtaining t=1/3.
2. DG is on BC: because D is already on y=0, only need G_y=0, namely 7-6t=0, obtaining t=7/6.
3. FG is on AB: because F is already on AB, only need G to satisfy y=3x/4, namely 7-6t=(3/4)(1+2t), solving gives 28-24t=3+6t, hence t=5/6.
4. EF is on AB: because F is already on AB, only need E to satisfy y=3x/4, namely 3t-1=(3/4)(7-t), solving gives 12t-4=21-3t, hence t=5/3.
These values are all within the movement time range 0<=t<=2. For a side to coincide with AC requires that both endpoints of the corresponding side are on the vertical line x=8; substituting the above coordinates gives no additional solution satisfying the movement range.
